questions.prompt: What is a major flaw described in current contrast mathematics?

options.text: It requires text to be extremely small to pass.
It treats light text on a dark background the same as dark text on a light background.
It only measures the color red.
It automatically fails any design that uses brand colors.

questions.explanation: The research says current math is not polarity-aware and does not model reverse polarity differently.
questions.hint: Think about how the method handles inverted colors.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Recognize the flaws in current contrast mathematics.

questions.prompt: What does it mean for a contrast algorithm to be polarity-aware?

options.text: It only works in freezing temperatures.
It uses different math depending on whether text is lighter or darker than the background.
It evaluates the emotional impact of a color palette.
It only evaluates black and white designs.

questions.explanation: A polarity-aware model treats light-on-dark differently from dark-on-light to better model perception.
questions.hint: It relates to which color is on top and which is on the bottom.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Understand how color polarity affects human perception.

questions.prompt: How does the proposed APCA account for font size?

options.text: It dictates that all fonts must be 12 pixels.
It generates scores that relate the color pair to the needed font size or thickness.
It forces mobile devices to zoom in automatically.

questions.explanation: The research describes APCA as spatially aware, tying contrast scores to typography details.
questions.hint: Think about how it pairs color scores with typography details.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Prepare for future, perceptually uniform contrast standards.
